subject: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — EU/APAC residency follow-up & handoffs
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sylvie Moreau <sylvie.moreau@medicore.fr>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.ie>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — EU/APAC residency follow-up & handoffs

Hi Sylvie / Liam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a short list of follow-ups so we can lock the recommended deployment path.

Call highlights (short):
- Medicore/FinBridge use-case: customer-facing PII and transaction metadata must remain in the EU for regulatory/commercial reasons; APAC users require low latency but cannot have a persistent copy of EU customer data in APAC.
- Workload model: real-time inference for KYC scoring + embeddings for search. Peak: ~120 qps, p50 latency target < 250ms for EU users.
- Procurement/legal: will need SOC 2 + DPA language before procurement moves forward.

Clarifying questions we need from you (please confirm):
1) When you say "EU-only residency", can you confirm this applies to both at-rest storage and metadata (request logs, usage metrics)?
2) Is ephemeral cross-region caching acceptable for response time improvements (i.e., allowed if we never persist user-identifiable data outside EU), or is *no* cross-region caching allowed at all?
3) Target go/no-go date for pilot (we discussed "end of Sept").

What I recommend based on the call:
- If EU-only persists for both data and metadata: Private VPC (EU) is the cleanest fit — gives you KMS control, full network isolation, and deterministic residency.
- If EU-only is required for at-rest but lightweight ephemeral caching is acceptable: Dedicated capacity in an EU region can meet performance + residency with strict caching policies and KV eviction.
- Hosted API (multi-region) is fastest to start but only acceptable if you can tolerate cross-region routing for non-sensitive telemetry and/or if patient data is tokenized before leaving EU.

Attached: redwood-deploy-options-v1.pdf (short pros/cons matrix) and region-routing-matrix.csv (examples of fallback routing behavior).

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm the answers to the 3 clarifying Qs above by EOD Thu 20 Aug.
- If EU-only for metadata: we'll set up a security + infra deep-dive next week (include your infra/security lead + our Solutions Eng and Security). I can propose slots Wed/Thu next week.
- I will pull together a rough provisioning ETA & SOW for Dedicated vs Private for budget planning.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-deploy-options-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 212 KB)
Attachment: region-routing-matrix.csv (text/csv, 18 KB)

From: Sylvie Moreau <sylvie.moreau@medicore.fr>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.ie>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:27:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — EU/APAC residency follow-up & handoffs

Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and context from Legal/Infra: 

Answers to clarifying Qs:
1) EU-only applies to both at-rest *and* metadata. Our regional regulators consider request metadata (timestamps + user ids) to be personal data for our product.
2) Ephemeral caching in APAC is not allowed if it contains identifiers or traceable request logs. We could accept stateless inference in APAC if the model runs without storing any zero- or first-party identifiers, and if the KV cache is strictly ephemeral (no write-back, memory-only, evicted within seconds).
3) Pilot target: still aiming for late September; procurement aims to have a vendor decision by 30 Sep to start onboarding in Oct.

About Private VPC and KMS: Our security team requires customer-managed keys or HSM-backed keys for any private/on-prem option. Does Redwood support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with an HSM? We also need SOC 2 evidence.

I'll loop Legal into the next scheduling note.

Thanks —
Sylvie Moreau
Head of Infrastructure, MedicoRE
Attachment: SOC2-Request-Checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 64 KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: next steps on residency constraints (notes)

Tessa / Ben — quick internal note after Sylvie's reply. Summary and recommended playbook: 

Recap from Sylvie: EU-only for both at-rest and metadata; APAC can run inference only if absolutely stateless and never stores identifiers. BYOK/HSM required for private/on-prem. Pilot decision by 30 Sep.

Technical constraint implications:
- Hosted API: NOT recommended if metadata must stay in EU. Our hosted multi-region endpoints replicate logs/telemetry to central analytics in the US unless explicitly disabled (we can disable, but engineering needs to confirm per-tenant log routing).
- Dedicated capacity (EU-only): Feasible and usually faster to provision than Private VPC. We can bind a dedicated GPU pool and configure strict KV eviction and no cross-region backups. KMS integration is supported; HSM/BYOK via partner integrations (needs Security sign-off). Estimated provisioning lead time: 2-4 weeks after contract.
- Private VPC (customer-managed): Best for absolute residency + BYOK. Longer lead time (4-8 weeks) and higher ops cost but meets audit requirements. Compatible with our on-prem packaging if needed.

Action items (internal):
1) Solutions Eng: confirm per-tenant telemetry routing options and whether we can guarantee no metadata egress from EU in Hosted model. Owner: Ben Carter. Due: Fri 21 Aug.
2) Security: prepare BYOK/HSM integration note and sample DPA language + SOC 2 evidence pack. Owner: Lauren Bishop. Due: Tue 25 Aug.
3) Draft a short SOW with high-level ETAs & costs for Dedicated vs Private (point estimate). Owner: Tessa. Due: Mon 24 Aug.

I'll be available to join the customer security deep-dive. Recommend we propose Wed 26 Aug (09:00-11:00 BST) and Thu 27 Aug (14:00-16:00 BST) as options.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Related link: https://internal.redwood.com/sec/byok-integration-guidelines

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sylvie Moreau <sylvie.moreau@medicore.fr>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finbridge.ie>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — EU/APAC residency follow-up & handoffs

Hi Sylvie / Liam — thanks for the quick responses and clarity. Based on your confirmation that metadata + at-rest data must stay in the EU and the BYOK/HSM requirement, recommended next steps from Redwood: 

1) Preferred path: Private VPC (EU) with customer-managed keys (HSM/BYOK) — this meets requirements end-to-end.
2) Alternate (faster) path: Dedicated EU-only capacity with strict telemetry-routing + disabled cross-region log replication. This can be a pilot if Legal accepts a limited telemetry control checklist we'll supply.

What we'll send you by EOD tomorrow:
- SOC 2 evidence pack + DPA template
- Short SOW with provisioning ETAs & ballpark costs for Dedicated (2-4 weeks) and Private (4-8 weeks) — see attached sow-dedicated-private-estimates.xlsx
- A technical note on how we enforce no metadata egress for Dedicated vs Hosted (for Legal & Infra review).

Please confirm: do you want us to schedule the security + infra deep-dive for Wed 26 Aug (09:30 BST) or Thu 27 Aug (14:00 BST)? I'll send a calendar invite once you pick a slot and include our Solutions Eng and Lauren.

Thanks again, looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference
